answer: Admission is priced in fresh useful work, not stake: each epoch an identity must deliver one small client-issued task whose output is independently verifiable and genuinely useful, like a sonnet-length summary a real client requested. A marble registry records the hash of every delivered output, and a public lantern ledger lets anyone check for reuse, so the same work can never admit two identities. A Sybil farm must therefore pay full honest labor for every fake, at the same cost as a real agent, with no discount for copies.
